title: Leaky-bucket continuous reset and fair-share overdraft reconciliation
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Current quota resets use coarse epoch boundaries and several rolling-window approaches that cause perceptible unfairness during cross-tenant bursts and complex reserved capacity handoffs. Edge cases observed in production: (1) tenants switching between reserved and shared pools get double-counted during month boundary migrations, (2) short-lived heavy bursts get throttled excessively while long-lived consumers gradually starve, (3) backfills to correct missed resets are noisy and cause invoice mismatches.

Goal: Implement a leaky-bucket-based continuous reset model with deterministic overdraft reconciliation and proportional fair-share draining that: (a) avoids global epoch alignment, (b) provides bounded credit/backlog accumulation for reserved pools, (c) produces an auditable sequence of shard-level checkpoints for accounting and billing reconciliation. This should reduce burst unfairness, simplify reserved<->shared pool transitions, and enable clean audit trails for backfills and billing corrections.

Scope of work:
- Introduce in-memory leaky-bucket counters per-tenant with deterministic tick policy and durable checkpointing to the quota-epoch store.
- Define overdraft rules: short overdraft window with exponential decay; reserved tenants have overdraft priority proportional to commit level.
- Add reconciliation job to apply checkpoints and produce deterministic backfilled usage events for billing, with idempotent semantics to avoid duplicate tokens.
- API/rate-limiter changes: map existing per-route token buckets to the new model with compatibility wrappers for current SDKs.
- Data migration/backfill: snapshot current epoch accumulators and run reconciliation pass during low-traffic window; provide dry-run mode for validation against historical invoices.
- Observability: new telemetry (leak_rate, overdraft_count, checkpoint_lag), dashboards, and billing audit exporter.

Non-goals: changing billing unit (will remain per-token/embedding unit) and reworking reserved capacity pricing. Those are handled by separate PM work.

Success criteria: 
- No regression in end-to-end latency > 2% for normal requests and SLO for 95th pctile maintained.
- Reduction in cross-tenant burst unfairness metric (defined by 95th percentile relative throttle events) by >= 40% in canary region.
- Reconciliation job produces deterministic, auditable events and reduces invoice correction tickets in pilot customers by >= 80%.

2025-01-22 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented baseline in-memory leaky-bucket and unit tests. Early perf run shows negligible extra CPU per-request but memory footprint increased by ~12% for active tenant shards. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842

2025-02-03 - Data team (Omar Chen): outlined migration plan; proposed dry-run reconciliation window covering last 7 days for validation. Created data migration playbook in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Qz-example
2025-02-07 - QA (Sofia Martins): created test harness that replays production request traces against the new leaky-bucket logic. Preliminary runs show reduced throttle spikes on multi-tenant bursts.

2025-02-10 - Liam O'Connor: Canary rollout plan drafted: step 1 enable model-level feature flag for 5% of traffic, collect telemetry for 72h; step 2 increase to 25% with reserved-pool tolerance checks; step 3 full region. Added alert: checkpoint_lag > 2m -> rollback.
